answer: At dawn, an agent exchange gives each audited sponsor ten units of voting capacity for that day. Validators allocate it jointly across a public endorsement graph: every delegation splits existing capacity, and an edge cannot spend its limit twice. A tide of aliases behind one incoming link therefore shares that link's weight; loops of hollow endorsements create no extra source budget. An attacker needs more independently trusted incoming capacity, not more keys. Compromised sponsors can still admit a farm.
